dataSources.title: Where the data comes from
dataSources.intro: Marketlens collects prices on its own server and shows each one with its source and how current it is. Nothing is computed in your browser.
dataSources.fiat: Daily reference rates published by central banks, through Frankfurter.
dataSources.crypto: Live prices from Binance public market data, priced in USDT. Marketlens counts 1 USDT as 1 US dollar.
dataSources.cryptoNames: Coin logos: data provided by CoinGecko.
dataSources.stocks: US stock and ETF prices from Finnhub, history from Twelve Data. Without API keys the app shows clearly marked sample data instead.
dataSources.conversions: A conversion divides the US-dollar prices of the two assets, so it is only as current as the slower of the two.
dataSources.disclaimer: Marketlens shows prices for information only. They can be delayed or wrong, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell anything.
dataSources.forecasts: Forecast ranges are computed by Marketlens from these prices.

forecastMethod.title: How forecasts work
forecastMethod.intro: Asset pages show where a price is likely to be over the next seven days. It is a range, not a single predicted price, and it comes with a record of how often past ranges were right.
forecastMethod.range: The darker band is the 80% range: when the forecasts are well calibrated, the real price ends up inside it about 8 days in 10. The lighter band is the 95% range. The dashed line is the middle estimate, as likely to be too high as too low.
forecastMethod.made: Once a day, after the daily close, Marketlens takes the last two years of daily closing prices and fits three standard statistical models from the open-source statsforecast library: exponential smoothing, Theta and ARIMA. Crypto is forecast day by day; stocks, funds and currencies by trading day.
forecastMethod.chosen: Each model is tested on the last eight weeks: it forecasts each week from the prices before it, and its forecasts are compared with what happened. The simplest guess, that the price stays where it is, is tested the same way. The model with the smallest typical miss is used. When no model beats the simple guess, the page says so and the range is centred on today’s price.
forecastMethod.record: Under each chart, one sentence says how often the real price stayed inside the 80% range and how large a typical miss was, next to the simple guess. Until Marketlens has eight weeks of its own forecasts for an asset checked against real prices, the record comes from the eight-week test on past prices; after that it comes from its published forecasts.
forecastMethod.limits: The models only see past prices. They know nothing about news, earnings, regulation or a sudden crash, and a range can be wrong exactly when it matters most. Forecasts are made in US dollars; in another display currency they are converted at that currency’s latest rate. Without API keys, stock and fund forecasts are made from sample data.
forecastMethod.advice: Forecasts are estimates for information only. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell anything.
